rows.coder_note: The FinnGen data are attributed to reference 18 (Kurki 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-022-05473-8), the source of every FinnGen release row; the passages give only endpoint case and control counts (10,413/308,633 and 9,511/362,581) and European descent, no release number, so no attribute separates the rows (rule E not met).

rows.quote: In the discovery stage, plasma protein pQTL data were obtained from the ARIC study, which included a total of 4657 plasma proteins collected from 7213 European Americans (EA) (17).
rows.reference_quote: Zhang J Dutta D Köttgen A Tin A Schlosser P Grams ME . Plasma proteome analyses in individuals of European and African ancestry identify cis-pQTLs and models for proteome-wide association studies . Nat Genet ( 2022 ) 54 ( 5 ): 593 – 602 . doi: 10.1038/s41588-022-01051-w 35501419 PMC9236177
rows.coder_note: The sentence attributes the ARIC pQTL data to reference 17 (DOI 10.1038/s41588-022-01051-w), whose source has two dictionary rows; '7213 European Americans (EA)' in the same sentence matches the European American row only (rule E). No conflicting release information.

rows.quote: For the replication stage, plasma protein pQTL data were obtained from the Icelandic deCODE genetics study by Ferkingstad et al, which analyzed 4907 plasma proteins from 35,559 Icelanders and reported more than 272 million genetic variants (16).
rows.reference_quote: Ferkingstad E Sulem P Atlason BA Sveinbjornsson G Magnusson MI Styrmisdottir EL . Large-scale integration of the plasma proteome with genetics and disease . Nat Genet ( 2021 ) 53 ( 12 ): 1712–21 . doi: 10.1038/s41588-021-00978-w 34857953
rows.coder_note: Rule I2: this row's own passage (abstract) gives only the cohort name; the sentence under row pqtl_1, passage p002, explicitly describes the Icelandic deCODE genetics replication dataset and attributes it to reference 16 (DOI 10.1038/s41588-021-00978-w), the source of one dictionary row; 35,559 Icelanders agrees with that row.
